subject: Onboarding: operational steps for 'no-training' commitment
messages:
From: Marisol Vega <marisol.vega@nexusretail.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@nexusretail.com
Date: 2026-09-09T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Nexus onboarding — confirm operational steps for 'no-training'

Hi Connor,

Thanks for the demo last week. As part of our DPA review we need to operationalize Nexus's 'no-training / no-model-improvement' requirement for the pilot. Legal asked for a short, actionable checklist we can hand to our security and procurement teams. Specifically they want to know:

- what runtime controls you provide to ensure customer inputs are not used for model updates;
- what evidence we can get (audit logs, attestations, config snapshots);
- how prompts/responses are treated (ownership, exportability); and
- the subprocessors that will see raw interaction data and where data can be routed (onshore/EU).

Can you share an onboarding playbook and a couple of sample artifacts we can attach to the DPA? Attachments or links would be great.

Best,
Marisol
Security Program Manager
Nexus Retail

Attachment: nexus_request_form.pdf (stub)

From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: Marisol Vega <marisol.vega@nexusretail.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-09T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nexus onboarding — confirm operational steps for 'no-training'

Hi Marisol — thanks for laying that out. Looping in Ops (Grace), Legal/Compliance (Laura) and Product (Aditya) so we can give a compact playbook and sample artifacts. High-level we can provide:

1) Runtime enforcement
- Dedicated request flagging: requests from Nexus pilot tenant will be routed to a no-training runtime slice where model-improvement hooks are disabled.
- KV/prefix caching: option to disable prefix-level caching and to scope KV cache to ephemeral-only (purged on session end).
- Telemetry filters: we can exclude specific token-level telemetry from logging; telemetry that remains for health is redacted.

2) Evidence artifacts
- Audit log extract (timestamped): token-level request hashes + routing decision for a configurable window.
- Configuration snapshot: runtime config showing "no_training": true, list of active subprocessors, and routing policy.
- Attestation letter from Redwood security describing the runtime controls and retention policy.

3) Data handling & ownership
- Prompt/response ownership: Nexus retains ownership of prompts and responses by default; Redwood provides exportable transcripts and an export SLA.
- Export options: SFTP or on-demand API export; recommended to use SFTP for batch retention windows.

4) Subprocessors & residency
- We will provide a current subprocessor roster and can gate certain subprocessors (e.g., analytics) behind onshore-only routing for Nexus.

I'm attaching a short checklist (nexus_no_train_checklist.xlsx) and our ops playbook excerpt. Grace — can you validate the operational steps and add any runbook items we should call out for onboarding? Laura — any legal artifacts you want packaged with the checklist?

Connor
Manager, Solutions
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Nexus onboarding — confirm operational steps for 'no-training'

Thanks — added a few operational specifics below that we should include in the playbook so customer's security teams can map to their controls:

- Ingestion path: All Nexus traffic will be labeled with tenant metadata and routed to the "no-train" serving pool. Routing is enforced at the load-balancer layer with policy tags; we can provide a sanitized routing policy JSON on request.
- KV purge: For interactive sessions we support immediate KV cache purge on session termination and a scheduled daily purge for ephemeral stores.
- Audit slices: We deliver audit slices as gzipped CSVs with hashed tokens + routing metadata; PII rows are redacted per Nexus policy. Retention window for these slices is configurable (default 30 days).
- Subprocessor gating: If Nexus requires, we can implement a gating rule that prevents analytics subprocessors from receiving raw transcripts — instead analytics events are aggregated on-prem or routed through an onshore partner.
- Export SLA: Standard export timeline is 48 hours; we can accelerate to 24 hours for pilot if procurement approves an operational uplift fee.

I recommend the onboarding checklist include a short "Required decisions" table for Nexus: export transport (SFTP/API), retention window, whether to enable prefix caching, and subprocessor gating. I'll prepare concrete runbook steps for the pilot kickoff.

Grace O'Connor
Sr. Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Legal: please also include a short paragraph that confirms Redwood will not use Nexus data to train models (no-weights-update) and reference the specific config flag and the attestation we expect at pilot completion.
- Security: we want the default export SLA to be 24 hours for pilot data (they will approve uplift). Please confirm onshore gating for analytics subprocessors and provide the subprocessor roster with countries for each.

Next steps: can we get the runbook steps and a sample audit slice by EOD Tuesday? Also please include a redlined example clause we can drop into the DPA that maps to the operational controls you described.

Marisol
Security Program Manager, Nexus Retail
